findings.desc: experiments/multi-model-ablation/m2-provider-execution-check.mjs:92 only rejects an exact outcome key or records path fields, while experiments/multi-model-ablation/m2-provider-execution-launch.json:8 declares containsOutcomeData=false and lines 22-23 declare no outcome/result rows. A launch artifact could add resultRows/outcomeRecords/phase1Results data without an outcome key and still pass, creating a false negative against the no-outcome-data boundary. Severity: medium.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit e1f2364024177f041754bce36677a20b2efa5e62. The checker now recursively rejects outcome/result-shaped launch data including resultRows, outcomeRecords, phase1Results, phase2Results, and presence flags such as resultRowsPresent/outcomeRecordsPresent/containsOutcomeData. Re-ran m2-provider-execution-check: PASS 391 assertions / 27 negative controls, plus m0/m1/m2 launch readiness checks.

findings.desc: experiments/multi-model-ablation/m2-provider-execution-check.mjs:183-190 validates only disabled flags and snapshot labels for providerLaunch.runnerAuthorization.runners, but it never requires the launch runner set to match phase1-runner-manifest.m2.json:194-231 or the launch rows at m2-provider-execution-launch.json:129-170. Removing a runner, changing a runnerId/cell binding, or adding an unrelated disabled runner can pass, so schema drift in the launch plan is a false negative. Severity: medium.
